metal-free S100A protein has been crystallized under the strict exclusion from oxygen and in the presence of metal-free SODA.

the structure of apo-S10A3 has been determined by MIRAS with two different heavy-atom derivatives.

the structural and functional characterization of S100A3 in the absence of metals and the elucidation of the structural differences to other S100 proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the metal-free apo-S100A structure is not the native state, but that the apo-state is a conformational state that is not accessible under physiological conditions and that it is a conformation that is stabilized by the crystal lattice.
apo-S100A proteins have an open conformation with an extended pseudo-EF-hand and an open canonical EF-hand.

apo-S100A proteins have a similar structure to that of apo-S100B and apo-S100A6, which is different from that of apo-SOD and apo-SCA1, and that the apo-S100 proteins have a different conformation from that of S100 proteins in the metal complex state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the apo-S100 structure is a good starting point for structure-based design of metal-free S-100A3 inhibitors.
the MIRAS phasings of apo-S100B and apo-S100A6 were successful and the apo-S100B structure was solved by SIRAS phasing.
the apo-S100 proteins are not in a metal-binding conformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MIRAS can be used to phase metal-free protein crystal structures, even in cases where metal binding induces conformational changes.
metal-free MIRAS can be a useful tool in cases of metal-sensitive proteins and in the absence or presence of a suitable heavy-metal derivative.
metal-free MIRAS is a very powerful tool for the phasing of protein structures.
